open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: “trial_executions: the TrialExecutions (M07) this admission ran” and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time” conflict with “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, is a new AdmissionVerdict created for the newly minted TrialExecutions, or is the existing verdict reused despite the required rerun?
options: Create a new verdict for every admission run, with identity including its fresh TrialExecutions
Reuse one verdict per implementation and corpus and reuse or replace its evidence
Separate the repeatable admission-run observation from the implementation-and-corpus verdict value
open_points.default_guess: Separate each admission run and its fresh TrialExecutions from a content-derived verdict keyed by implementation and corpus.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with “the proof refuses a binding that is not accepted” and the OperationBinding lifecycle “proposed → accepted.”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can fail proof while a referenced binding is proposed and later pass after that binding is accepted?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant binding states or proof context
ProofResult is only an ephemeral observation and has no stable identity by flow version
A flow version's first proof result is permanent, so later binding acceptance cannot change it
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computation as an ephemeral result whose facts may change with binding state; do not define equality solely by flow_version_id.

open_points.subject: Run and draft-write authority
open_points.text: M26 requires “the flow activation under which the run started” and identifies it “by its position in the store's order,” but M19 pins only “flow_version_id” and “pinned_implementations.”
open_points.question: How does a run retain the exact FlowActivation that authorizes its draft-write sends, especially if the same version is activated multiple times or activation changes before the node sends?
options: Store the exact FlowActivation reference on Run at start
Store the FlowActivation reference only in each EffectAttempt using execution-time reconstruction
Derive the activation retrospectively from global store ordering and the run's creation position
open_points.default_guess: Pin the exact FlowActivation reference on the Run when it starts and copy that reference into each applicable EffectAttempt.

open_points.subject: Mapped node port cardinality
open_points.text: M01 says “`many` is what a map runs over,” while M14 says “`map_over`: the one input port a `many` edge maps the node over” and “each output collects one result per element.”
open_points.question: What are the declared and effective cardinalities on a mapped node's input and outputs: does a `many` source feed a `one` input per execution and promote outputs to `many`, or must the node's own ports be declared `many`?
options: A `many` source maps into a `one` node input; each declared `one` output becomes an effective `many` flow result
The mapped input and outputs themselves must be declared `many`
Both declared cardinalities are allowed, with defined nesting or flattening semantics
open_points.default_guess: Use mapping as a cardinality adapter: a `many` source supplies one element to a `one` input per execution, and per-execution outputs are collected as effective `many` outputs.
